title: How Fast Can a Performance Model Actually Be Built? - Semiwiki
gist: Simplex Micro and CircuitSutra built an RTL-correlated scalar-vector RISC-V performance model in about three months by reusing a portable modeling methodology, and are pitching fast model-extension (3-5 weeks per new microarchitecture) plus a self-service IPC visualization tool as differentiators for teams evaluating RISC-V IP.

insights.claim: Simplex Micro and CircuitSutra built an RTL-correlated scalar-vector performance model for a RISC-V core in about three months: starting April 2026, the pipeline model was substantially written by six weeks, real workloads (Dhrystone and a matrix-multiplication VPU benchmark) were running with actual IPC figures by eight weeks, and by twelve weeks Dhrystone correlation against RTL was complete with branch misprediction and L1 cache miss behavior matching RTL trace data exactly.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: A roughly 12-week start-to-RTL-validation timeline is a concrete benchmark for judging how fast a performance-modeling vendor or in-house team can deliver a validated model for a new core.
insights.quote: By twelve weeks in, that wasn’t just running — it was correlated: Dhrystone correlation against RTL was complete, and branch misprediction and L1 cache miss behavior matched RTL trace data exactly.
insights.locator: Work began on the performance model in April 2026

insights.claim: Once the base modeling methodology is established, extending the performance model to cover new components like L2 cache and a full vector processing unit is estimated at three to five weeks, with three weeks realistic once the hard architectural questions are resolved early.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Reusable modeling frameworks that extend in weeks rather than months could materially shorten performance-validation cycles for follow-on RISC-V microarchitecture variants.
insights.quote: the estimate for adding L2 cache modeling and a full VPU model landed at three to five weeks, with three weeks being the realistic target once the harder architectural questions are worked through early rather than left for later
insights.locator: That’s what makes extending the model to cover new components

themes.theme: Reusable methodology as the speed enabler

insights.claim: The model's speed comes from a reusable base structure covering pipeline behavior, branch prediction, cache hierarchy, and instruction timing that can be ported to a new microarchitecture rather than rebuilt from scratch each time.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: A portable modeling methodology signals a scalable, productizable process that lowers the marginal cost of validating each new core variant.
insights.locator: Why Speed Is Possible: A Reusable Foundation, Not a Rebuild

insights.claim: The performance model shares its instruction decode table directly with the RTL, so adding or modifying an instruction is reflected in both simultaneously, which significantly cuts the ongoing correlation effort needed to keep model and RTL in sync.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: A shared decode-table design reduces model/RTL drift risk and is a concrete engineering detail worth checking when assessing any vendor's cycle-accuracy claims.
insights.quote: sharing the instruction decode table between the performance model and the RTL wherein adding or modifying an instruction reflects in both the performance model and the RTL and the correlation effort is significantly less
insights.locator: The modeling starts with the concept of sharing the instruction decode table

insights.claim: The performance-modeling approach is described as simple enough that a new engineering graduate with computer-architecture knowledge and C++ skills can build a performance model.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: If accurate, this lowers the talent and cost barrier to building custom performance models in-house, a potential competitive pressure on third-party EDA performance-modeling tools.
insights.quote: the performance modeling concept is fairly simple in such a way that a new grad who understand computer architecture and C++ programming skill can build a performance model.
insights.locator: The important factor is the simplicity of the performance modeling foundation

insights.claim: The team surfaces difficult modeling problems immediately and, if not critical to the near-term milestone, explicitly defers low-importance/high-difficulty items to a later phase rather than letting them silently slip the schedule.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: A surface-early, defer-explicitly triage discipline is a transferable project-management lesson for any hardware/software co-validation effort running on an aggressive timeline.
insights.quote: Anything considered low-importance and high-difficulty gets pushed to a later phase explicitly, keeping the core timeline intact instead of blocked on edge cases.
insights.locator: Part of what keeps that timeline honest is sequencing

insights.claim: Benchmarks were validated one at a time in sequence (Dhrystone, then matrix multiplication, then TinyML and Qwen), with correlation against RTL chased down at the cycle-by-cycle level for each benchmark rather than declared complete via aggregate IPC or ratio comparisons.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Cycle-accurate, benchmark-by-benchmark correlation is a stronger validation bar than aggregate IPC matching and a useful diligence criterion for comparing performance-model vendors.
insights.quote: It is not correlating that the IPC and the ratio numbers, but the actual cycle-by-cycle correlation.
insights.locator: This is the same discipline visible in the benchmark rollout

insights.claim: By the time it was shown externally, the model already covered the full scalar-and-vector compute engine and was validated against real workloads including TinyML and Qwen, making it a working tool a design team can point its own workload at immediately rather than a roadmap pitch.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: A demo-ready, workload-validated model is a stronger sales and diligence signal for prospective RISC-V IP licensees than a promised roadmap.
insights.quote: it’s “here’s a model you can point your own workload at today.”
insights.locator: The Payoff: A Demo-Ready Model, Fast

insights.claim: The performance model ships with documentation letting a design team run it independently; this contrasts with RTL-based exploration, where testing a configuration change requires going back to whoever owns the re-synthesis flow and waiting a multi-day turnaround, versus minutes with the self-service model.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Self-service performance modeling can cut design-space-exploration turnaround from multi-day RTL re-synthesis cycles to minutes, a meaningful productivity lever when evaluating cache size or issue-width tradeoffs.
insights.quote: exploring a configuration change in RTL means going back to whoever owns the re-synthesis flow and waiting on a multi-day turnaround. With a documented, self-service performance model, a design team can test a cache size or issue-width change on their own, in minutes.
insights.locator: Speed only matters if the result is usable by someone other than the team that built it

insights.claim: CircuitSutra built an IPC Visualization tool that plots per-cycle IPC across an entire run with dynamically color-coded instruction classes (ALU, branch, vector, vector load, vector store, CSR, divide, load, multiply, store), letting a design team see at a glance whether execution is scalar-bound, vector-bound, load-bound, or branch-heavy.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Visual, instruction-class-level bottleneck attribution beyond a single aggregate IPC number is a differentiator worth weighing when comparing performance-analysis tools for RISC-V vector cores.
insights.quote: plots per-cycle IPC across an entire run and a dynamically color-coded instruction classes — ALU, branch, vector, vector load, vector store, CSR, divide, load, multiply, store
insights.locator: The IPC Visualization tool, shown below

insights.claim: The visualization includes a dedicated miss-event track flagging D-cache misses and branch mispredictions cycle by cycle (including overlapping same-cycle events), with zoomable IPC plots that drill into an instruction-level trace table showing issue, execute, writeback, and retire down to the specific program counter, exportable to Excel.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: PC-level trace drill-down with Excel export makes root-cause performance debugging accessible to design teams without custom tooling, a practical usability checkpoint for evaluating the model.
insights.quote: flagging D-cache misses and branch mispredictions cycle by cycle, including cycles where both occur in the same cycle
insights.locator: A dedicated miss-event track sits directly beneath it

insights.claim: The performance model is built on the RISC-V open-source compiler and the Whisper instruction set simulator, meaning any design team can use it with the right C library and Linux version rather than needing proprietary tooling.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Reliance on open-source RISC-V compiler and simulator tooling lowers the adoption barrier and vendor lock-in risk for teams evaluating Simplex Micro's IP.
insights.quote: Our performance model uses the RISC-V open-source compiler and Whisper Instruction in which any design team can use with the right c library and Linux version.
insights.locator: Why This Matters for RISC-V IP Designers

insights.claim: The authors position model-extension speed itself as core to their pitch to RISC-V IP evaluators: a model extensible in weeks rather than quarters can keep pace with a design team's own exploration, turning the performance model from a static deliverable into a living tool that evolves with the architecture.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Evaluators of RISC-V IP vendors should weigh performance-model iteration speed as a differentiator alongside raw PPA numbers.
insights.quote: It’s the difference between a performance model as a static deliverable and a performance model as a living tool that evolves alongside the architecture it’s describing.
insights.locator: For designers evaluating RISC-V IP, the speed of the performance model isn’t a side detail
